ROOT_CAUSE:
The attribution recorders of WB-1002-11 and WB-1002-13 only ever fire on the ADB path. `build_router` (executor_router.py:257) binds the MAA executor's resolver to `lambda semantic: router.maa_resolver(semantic, skill_id)`, which never passes through the runtime's `resolve`, so every miss decided inside `maa_resolver` was computed and then thrown away.

The day's ledger divides on that one fact rather than statistically. Of the 31 SEMANTIC_TARGET_NOT_VERIFIED rows whose revision carried the field:

    reason EMPTY (12) : OPEN_HOME 6, OPEN_BUILDING_UPGRADE 4, OPEN_TASK_FROM_QUICK_PANEL_HERO_RECRUIT 2
                        -- all three carry an MAA recognition node
    reason NAMED (19) : SELECT_RESOURCE 15, SELECT_BEAST_TARGET_MAMMOTH 3, TRY_ORDINARY_CONTROL 1
                        -- all three are node-less and fall through to adb_resolver

All four node-bearing skills measured dispatch as TEMPLATE (`dispatch_hint`), with gate [0.7, 0.75], which is exactly the branch that returned None in silence.

The vocabulary was already being computed one layer down: `MaaExecutorAdapter.match_template` returns a `RecognitionOutcome` on a miss carrying `error` (NO_MATCH / TEMPLATE_NOT_REGISTERED:<name> / MAA_NO_RECOGNITION_NODE / NO_FRAME / MAA_RECO_FAILED:<Exc>), `algorithm`, and the measured `score` of its best candidate *even when it did not hit*. `maa_resolver` held that object in `last_outcome` and read only `center_norm()`.

AFTER.why_the_score_and_not_only_a_name: 'reached 0.615 against a 0.70 gate' and 'the template was never loaded' send the next reader to two different fixes, and the first also says whether the answer is to move the gate or to replace the crop. A reason without the number cannot tell them apart.
AFTER.deliberately_preserved: One reason still survives a resolved point: the LIST_DYNAMIC fallback keeps LIST_DYNAMIC:NO_ROWS when the template then answers. That is pinned by test_rally_list_dynamic_node, and it means something worth keeping -- a template answering on a frame its own reader rejects is a node drifting apart from the screen -- so a success row carrying that code is not a live failure. Everywhere else a resolution clears the field, because runtime writes it into every episode row including successful ones.

VERIFIER_RESULT:
Wiring proven; live values NOT observed, and stated as such.

Proven: 10 tests red-first (5 of them failing on HEAD bytes); a byte-exact A/B both ways; the neighbouring set; check_wiring problems=0; invariant_review 10 PASS / 0 FAIL. The deployed revision 61adba7 went live about one minute after the repin and was confirmed running by its own episodes.

Not proven: that a real node-bearing miss now writes the new codes. The 8-minute observation window produced 20 episodes on 61adba7 and every single one was SUCCESS -- 0 failures, 0 SEMANTIC_TARGET_NOT_VERIFIED, the whole window being INTEL work (OPEN_INTEL / SELECT_INTEL_PIN / INTEL_*_START_MARCH / INTEL_HERO_DISPATCH). No node-bearing skill was reached, so there was nothing to judge. The three judgeable signals for the next reading: a FAILURE under one of the three node-bearing skills whose recognition_error starts with MAA_TEMPLATE: / MAA_FRAME:; a SEMANTIC_TARGET_NOT_VERIFIED under those skills with an empty reason (which would mean the hole is still open somewhere not covered); and the disappearance of empty reasons from the day's distribution.

EVIDENCE.the_division: The 31 rows split by one fact -- whether the skill has an MAA recognition node -- with no overlap: every empty reason belongs to a node-bearing skill and every named one to a node-less skill. That is what makes this a binding problem rather than a missing-feature problem.
EVIDENCE.the_binding: executor_router.py:253-259 shows the MAA executor built with `target_resolver=lambda semantic: router.maa_resolver(semantic, skill_id)`, and 378 `def maa_resolver` is a separate method from the runtime's `resolve`. The runtime's two recorders (runtime._resolution_error and runtime._router_recognition_error) therefore only ever see work the MAA resolver did.
EVIDENCE.the_three_silent_sites: maa_resolver returned None with nothing written at (a) `if frame is None`, (b) the LIST_DYNAMIC fallback with nothing usable to fall back to, and (c) the template path -- `self.last_outcome = outcome; return outcome.center_norm()` -- which is the default branch for every TEMPLATE node and therefore the one the measured skills take.
EVIDENCE.the_vocabulary_already_existed: maa_executor.match_template builds RecognitionOutcome(..., score=..., error=...) on the miss path too (lines 664-680), reading `best_result.score` regardless of `hit`; and 638 shows TEMPLATE_NOT_REGISTERED:<name> as its own error, distinct from NO_MATCH.
EVIDENCE.deliberately_not_measured: The real scores would require a second MaaFramework tasker against the emulator while AUTO is running. This project has already measured ADB/MAA contention on this machine, so the device was left alone and the values are left to the ledger.

REMAINING_ISSUE:
Four.

(a) The live values are unobserved (see VERIFIER_RESULT). The wiring is proven, the numbers are not yet read from a real frame.

(b) `MAA_TEMPLATE:` is now the only place that carries a score. The OCR path (`MAA_OCR:*`) still reports only the failure kind, not the OCR confidence it saw, so the same 'how close was it' question stays unanswered there. Measured worth: MAA_OCR:NO_TEXT on a real frame cannot be told apart from a near-miss on a mis-cropped ROI.

(c) A reason survives a resolved point in exactly one place (the LIST_DYNAMIC fallback). That is pinned and deliberate, but it means a SUCCESS row can carry a non-empty recognition_error, so any consumer that reads the column as 'did this step fail' is wrong. Worth writing down where consumers live.
